title: Sanctions Screening and Targeted Financial Sanctions
summary: Screen customers and counterparties against sanctions and PEP lists, handle matches, and freeze without delay as the UAE targeted financial sanctions regime requires.

lessons.title: Why sanctions screening matters
lessons.body:
## Funds that must not move

**Targeted financial sanctions (TFS)** require that the funds and assets of listed persons and entities are **frozen without delay**, and that no funds are made available to them.

The lists include persons designated by the **UN Security Council** and those on the **UAE local terrorist list**. TFS cover terrorism and the **financing of weapons proliferation**.

For an exchange house the risk is direct: a transfer sent to or from a listed party is a breach, even if the amount is small. Screening and freezing must happen **without delay**.

*Training summary of the CBUAE Rulebook. Always check the current Rulebook text and your own policy manual.*

lessons.title: Screening in practice
lessons.body:
## What and when to screen

Screen:

- The **customer**, the **beneficial owners** and authorised persons.
- The **beneficiary** and the **sender** of a transfer, and any counterparty.
- At **onboarding**, before **each transaction**, and again whenever the lists are **updated**.

A system often returns **possible matches**. Compare name, date of birth, nationality and identity number to decide whether it is a **true match** or a **false positive**. Never clear a hit by guessing: if you are unsure, **escalate to the Compliance Officer** and do not process the transaction.

lessons.title: Freezing without delay and reporting
lessons.body:
## A confirmed match

When a match is **confirmed**:

1. **Do not process** the transaction and do not release any funds.
2. **Freeze** the funds or assets without delay.
3. **Report** immediately through the channels set by the Compliance Officer, including the competent authorities.
4. **Do not tell the customer** more than your procedure allows.

Every LEH must register with the FIU's **Integrated Enquiries Management System (IEMS)** to receive and answer information requests. The legal basis is the TFS framework of Cabinet Decision No. 74 of 2020 and the guidance of the Executive Office for Control and Non-Proliferation.

*Training summary of the CBUAE Rulebook. Always check the current Rulebook text and your own policy manual.*

lessons.title: PEPs and adverse media
lessons.body:
## People with influence

A **politically exposed person (PEP)** holds, or has held, a prominent public role. Their **family members** and **close associates** are treated the same way, as is any company whose beneficial owner is a PEP.

Being a PEP is not a crime, but it carries higher corruption risk. Apply **EDD** at any transaction value: source of funds, reason for the transaction and senior-level approval under your procedures.

**Adverse media** means credible reports linking a customer to crime. A material adverse media hit can justify a suspicious activity report.

lessons.title: Video: FATF Recommendation 12 on PEPs
lessons.body:
## Before you watch

Recommendation 12 of the Financial Action Task Force sets the international standard for politically exposed persons. Watch it after the PEP reading and compare it with the steps your exchange house takes.

## Look out for

- Who counts as a PEP, and why family and close associates matter
- Why a PEP is higher risk but not automatically a criminal
- The extra steps taken before dealing with a PEP

## After watching

Answer the short quiz to move on.

*This video is made by a third party and opens on YouTube. It is not produced by Data Mine Labs or the CBUAE, and it may describe rules from other countries. Where it differs from the CBUAE Rulebook or your own policy manual, follow those.*

lessons.title: Keeping a trail
lessons.body:
## Prove what you did

For every alert, keep a record of:

- What was screened, against which lists and when.
- Who reviewed it and why it was cleared or escalated.
- Any freeze, report or decision.

These records must be kept for **at least five years** and shown to the CBUAE on request. An alert that was cleared without a written reason is a finding waiting to happen.

*Training summary of the CBUAE Rulebook. Always check the current Rulebook text and your own policy manual.*
